Area Forecast Discussion...UPDATED
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
1034 AM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Winter Weather Advisories have been issued for portions of the
Alleghenies for accumulating snow, some icing, and strong wind
gusts. Coastal Flood Warnings continue for most of the shoreline
of the Chesapeake Bay and Potomac River. Coastal Flood Warning
for Baltimore was dropped earlier. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Moderate tidal flooding persists, with accumulating
  mountain snow this afternoon into tonight.

- 2) Another potent area of low pressure brings precipitation 
  Sunday night into Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Moderate tidal flooding persists, with accumulating 
mountain snow this afternoon into tonight.

A potent and large area of low pressure over the central 
Appalachians this morning is going to steadily track north/east 
today, eventually pushing away from the area tonight into the 
weekend. The tight surface pressure gradient still in place and 
overall strength of the low will result in gusty conditions this 
morning and afternoon. This time winds are going to be out of the 
southwest, but certainly not as strong as yesterday. Peak gusts this 
afternoon are going to be around 25-35 mph, and up to 40-50 mph in 
the highest ridges of the Alleghenies. Seasonal temperatures in the 
40s to mid 50s as abundant cloud cover eventually starts to clear 
late this afternoon to evening. 

A Winter Weather Advisory has been issued for western Grant and 
western Pendleton Counties from this afternoon through Saturday 
morning. In most cases where southwesterly flow prevails the snow 
totals usually underperform in the mountains since there isn't 
enough moisture. However, the area of low pressure over the OH 
Valley remains potent and has ample low-level moisture feeding 
orographically forced showers in the mountains. Marginal surface 
temperatures through this afternoon result in a rain/snow mix that 
eventually transitions to all snow late afternoon into tonight. 
Around 3 inches of snow is likely at elevations above 3000 feet, and 
some locally higher amounts up to 4 inches are possible. At lower 
elevations down to 1000 feet a coasting to an inch or two is 
possible. As the area of low pressure departs tonight and warmer air 
moves in aloft, a light freezing drizzle develops Saturday morning 
in the Advisory area before precip comes to an end. 

Elsewhere, dry conditions are expected Saturday as ample sunshine 
returns. Slightly warmer temperatures in the 50s to low 60s.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Another potent area of low pressure brings 
precipitation Sunday night into Monday. 

High pressure will keep the region dry Sunday. Temperatures will be 
near seasonable with highs middle 50s to lower 60s.

As the high pushes further to the southeast Sunday night, a low 
pressure system will move from the middle Mississippi Valley on 
Sunday toward the eastern Great Lakes Sunday night. A trailing cold 
front will push across the region Sunday night into Monday morning.
Showers will likely accompany the front. We can't rule out a clap of 
thunder or two either given that there will be plenty of wind shear, 
despite instability being minimal to nil and the time of night for 
frontal passage. Highs cooler Sunday with highs mainly in lower to 
upper 50s.

Once the front moves to the east and southeast Monday afternoon, 
high pressure will become reestablished and bring dry conditions 
and seasonable temperatures to the region Monday through 
Wednesday.

&&

.AVIATION /15Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Expect at least a broken MVFR cloud deck to persist through the
afternoon before VFR conditions return. Main impacts today are 
going to be from southwest winds gusting around 25-30 knots at 
times. Winds diminish this evening, but gust around 20-25 knots 
again Saturday afternoon. 

VFR conditions Sunday. MVFR or IFR conditions possible Sunday night 
and Monday morning with front and showers and/or thunder. VFR 
conditions return Monday afternoon and Monday night. Winds variable 
becoming southeast 5 to 10 knots Sunday, increasing south to 
southwest 10 to 15 knots gusts 20 knots Sunday night, shifting 
northwest 10 to 20 knots gusts 25 knots Monday with frontal
passage.

&&

.MARINE...
Southwesterly winds ramp up this morning and afternoon as a strong 
upper low pressure tracks just west of the local waters. Gale 
Warnings are in effect for most waters, except the middle and upper 
tidal Potomac where Small Craft Advisory is in effect. Some guidance 
has Gales persisting into this evening, and that may require an 
extension of the Gale Warning for the middle bay. Otherwise, SCA 
conditions persist into Saturday, then winds finally diminish below 
SCA levels Saturday night into Sunday morning.

Small craft advisories look increasingly likely late Sunday into 
Sunday night with approaching front. Once the front passes later 
Sunday night or early Monday, then Gales could be possible with a 
gusty northwest wind. Small craft advisories look likely. Winds 
southeast 5 to 15 knots Sunday, then south to southwest 15 to 20 
knots Sunday night, shifting northwest 15 to 25 knots gusts up to 30 
knots Monday.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Moderate tidal flooding is expected to continue at many locations 
along the Chesapeake Bay and Potomac River through this afternoon's 
high tide cycle. After that anomalies decrease tonight into the 
weekend.

&&
